content:
As AI agents requiring "full disk access" permissions proliferate on Mac, Apple says it will make changes to macOS to protect user privacy.

While the company has not yet revealed specifics, Apple says users should understand what granting such "special" access permissions to apps means.

In a blog post on its developer website, Apple explained that "full disk access" in macOS is meant to "let backup apps work properly on Mac." However, Apple said "a few developers" are using macOS's "full disk access" setting in ways that "could put users at risk."

In response, Apple said it will "introduce additional controls to ensure users who genuinely wish to grant this special access to an app must do so through a very explicit user action."

The company has not provided any further details about these controls or the planned changes. Nonetheless, Apple said the rise of "increasingly powerful and autonomous" AI agents calls for greater attention to privacy and security:

Apple's announcement today comes amid the growing prevalence of tools like Meta Muse and OpenAI Dots. These always-on AI agents request access to a substantial amount of your personal data, and we have already seen some scary incidents, particularly with Meta Muse.
